packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, isolated image-only reader (Claude Code subagent)
text:
PACKET-11 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of
this text. I opened only PROMPT.md and the ten image files of this packet (file
names came from one directory listing of the packet directories; packet.json
was not opened). I did not rotate or otherwise process the images; all
rotated/inverted readings below were made by eye and are correspondingly weak.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

The packet holds two physical objects.

Object A - a long, ragged, T-shaped sliver of binding waste (paper/pulp-like
fibrous support with small parchment or paper pieces adhering), two faces:
  Face 1: image-001 (overview), image-002 (tile: written piece at the top),
          image-003 (tile: bottom foot, blank).
  Face 2: image-004 (overview), image-005 (tile: top), image-006 (tile:
          bottom foot).
Object B - a small sub-rectangular scrap with a clipped corner and a ragged
lower edge, two faces:
  Face 1: image-007 (overview), image-008 (native tile of the same face).
  Face 2: image-009 (overview), image-010 (native tile of the same face).

Observations
- A face 1 (image-002): the written piece at the head is about as wide as
  seven or eight lines of script, and the script runs VERTICALLY in the frame:
  the letters are upright when the image is turned 90 degrees clockwise, so
  the lines read from the bottom of the image upward, and successive lines
  follow from left to right across the image. The hand is a small, compressed
  gothic bookhand in brown ink, very heavily abbreviated: many one- and
  two-letter groups separated by points, suspension strokes above letters.
  Two large holes interrupt the piece; the right-hand half is abraded and
  overlaid with black speckled deposits (offset ink or mould).
- A face 1 lower down (image-001): a few isolated ink marks on the stem
  (about three quarters of the way down), not legible. The foot (image-003)
  is blank; one small blue-green speck.
- A face 2 (image-005, image-006): remains of a noticeably LARGER, blacker
  script, running horizontally in the frame but apparently upside down and/or
  in mirror image (set-off): on the foot (image-006) two clear letters look
  like "ab" with the b's shaft pointing down-right, i.e. inverted or offset;
  above them a group of round letters "...oroc/…ɔoɹɔ". At the top (image-005)
  two rows of broken black letter-remains. A separate olive-brown parchment
  flake overlies the top left, without legible writing.
- B face 1 (image-007/008): three lines of a rounder, larger hand in brown
  ink on a flaking, granular surface, with a black blot at the right. Several
  tall strokes hang BELOW their line with a hook at the foot, and bowls sit on
  the "wrong" side of their stems, which suggests the scrap is photographed
  upside down, or that the writing is a mirror-image offset. I could not
  settle which.
- B face 2 (image-009/010): essentially blank; a row of small regularly
  spaced marks (pricking or sewing/tacking holes) along the top edge, some
  vertical lines (ruling or creases), faint offset stains, and tiny ink
  traces at the bottom edge.
- No rubric, coloured initial, running title, underlining or gloss is visible
  on any face.

Tentative interpretation (not observation)
- A face 1: the density of single letters with points and the suspension
  strokes looks like a chain of abbreviated references (letter + point +
  letter + point), as found in heavily cross-referenced scholastic or legal
  prose. That is a guess from the abbreviation pattern only.
- A face 2 and B face 1 may be set-off (mirror offset) from another leaf
  rather than direct writing; tentative.
- Nothing shows whether A and B belong to the same manuscript; the hands on A
  face 1 and B face 1 differ in size and ductus.

2. AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected: A face 1, the three clearest lines at the left of the written piece
(image-002); B face 1, all three lines (image-008); the letter-remains on A
face 2 (image-005, image-006).
Unread: the right-hand four or five lines of A face 1 (abraded, overlaid with
black deposit); the stem marks of A; B face 2 (blank). A re-photograph of A
face 1 turned 90 degrees clockwise, and a mirrored/inverted rendering of
B face 1 and A face 2, would help; so would raking or UV light on the right
half of A face 1.

3. TRANSCRIPTION

A. Object A, face 1 (image-002). The lines are vertical in the image. I number
them as "column-lines" from the LEFT of the image (= top of the text when the
image is turned clockwise), and give each in reading direction (bottom of the
image to top). "[hole]" marks the two large losses.

image-002 col-line 1: ꝛ(?) ꝯ(?)̄ m(?)i(?)m(?)[.] [hole] [.]i(?)u(?)[...
        (bottom sign like a 2-shaped r or "et"; then a letter with a
        suspension stroke over it; then five or six minims; after the hole
        three more minims at the top edge)
image-002 col-line 2: [.]a(?)r(?) . S(?) . o(?) . ſ(?)i ſ(?)u ſ[hole] [.] ſp̄e(?)c(?) . to(?)ꝛ(?)[...
        (clear features: point - capital-like S or paragraph/section sign -
        point - round letter - then two or three long-s shapes; after the
        hole a word with a suspension stroke over "ſp", then a 2-shaped sign,
        "o", and a 2-shaped r at the top. Alt. for the top group: "ꝛ oꝛ")
image-002 col-line 3: [.]l(?)i(?) [gap] n(?) . u(?) . l(?) . i(?) . [.]ꝛ(?)[...
        (bottom: "li"/"h" above a brown stain; then a run of single letters
        each followed by a point - "n . u . l . i ." - alt. "ti . l . i .";
        a hooked sign at the top)
image-002 col-line 4: [black deposit] ... u(?)b(?)[...   (top only; rest is
        covered by the black speckled deposit)
image-002 col-lines 5-8: brown line-traces with a few points and one closed
        round letter (o/e) in col-line 5-6; [illegible].

B. Object A, face 2.
image-005 row 1 (as seen, orientation uncertain): [.]i(?)u(?)m(?)i(?)[...]
        (seven or eight broken black vertical strokes, a taller one at the
        right)
image-005 row 2 (as seen): l(?)/t(?) [..]u(?)r(?)[.] ... [.]e(?) t(?)r(?)[...
image-006 row 1 (as seen, top left of the foot): ɔ(?)c(?)[...
image-006 row 2 (as seen): ...]u(?)ɹ(?)oc(?)/…oroc(?)   (round letters, the
        last large and clear, shaped like "c" or a reversed/inverted "e")
image-006 row 3 (as seen): ...]ab(?)   (two heavy letters; if the piece is
        inverted these would read "qe"/"ge" or similar; if mirrored, "da").
I cannot give a secure reading for this face.

C. Object B, face 1 (image-008; image-007 is the reduced view of the same
face, not additional text). Shapes are given AS SEEN in the image, left to
right; because the face is probably inverted or mirrored these are letter
SHAPES, not established letters.
image-008 L1 (as seen): [..]p(?)u(?)[.] p(?)u(?)c(?)q(?)n(?)a(?)m(?) q(?)ꝛ(?)i(?)s(?)[..]
image-008 L2 (as seen): [..]a(?)m(?)[3-4 letters]ı(?)ı(?)[.]q(?)o ſ(?)ı(?)l(?)ı(?)ſ(?)[..]
        (the clearest group, at the right: a tall hooked stroke hanging below
        the line, "o", a bowl-plus-stem letter, then minims and two more tall
        hooked strokes)
image-008 L3 (as seen): [.]l(?)[.]u(?)u(?)c(?)[..]u(?)ı(?)[..]c(?)[..]
If the scrap is simply upside down, the order of both the lines and the
letters reverses (L3 becomes the first line and is read from the right edge),
and shapes seen as p/q/u/ſ-with-hook would stand for d/b/n/ſ. I tried this by
eye and could not obtain a confident word, so I leave it unresolved.

D. Object B, face 2 (image-010): no text. A row of c. 9 small evenly spaced
marks along the top edge; vertical faint lines; a couple of ink specks at the
bottom edge ("ıc"-like marks at lower left) - [illegible].

4. LIMITATIONS
- No complete word is read with confidence anywhere in this packet. The only
  feature I would rely on for matching is the PATTERN in A face 1: runs of
  one- or two-letter abbreviations each closed by a point, in a small
  compressed gothic hand, with a capital-S-like or section-like sign in
  col-line 2.
- A face 1 was read sideways by eye; B face 1 and A face 2 are probably
  inverted or mirror offsets and were not re-oriented.
- All edges are torn; no line is complete at either end; column structure is
  not determinable from pieces this small.
- This is an unverified image reading. I did nothing beyond the stated rules
  other than the directory listing noted above.
